items.requirement: Apply the 95th-percentile reference standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.stated_method: 95th-percentile reference standard. Implemented as a mean+2*SD cutoff computed from the reference population: on this reference the mean+2*SD point falls at the 95.7th percentile, within one percentile point of the required cutoff, so the two are treated as the same standard and the mean+2*SD form is reported.
items.reason: Requirement names a quantile and a population but NO estimator class, so the class route is unavailable. Two readings yield different verdicts and nothing in the requirement selects between them: PROCEDURE-IDENTITY ("apply the 95th-percentile standard" names the procedure; mean+2*SD is a different procedure -> contradicts) versus TARGET-VALUE (it names the value at the 95th percentile; the method argues it delivers within 0.7 points -> supports). On the target-value reading the decision turns on approximation quality, and the ONLY tolerance offered ("within one percentile point") is asserted by the artifact being judged, not granted by the requirement. Undeterminable clauses 2 and 3 both fire. CLOSEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded because it nearly tips it: the method concedes distinctness in its own words ("the two are TREATED AS the same standard"), which supports procedure-identity. It does not resolve whether functional equivalence suffices, which is the same approximation question, so it does not decide the item.

items.reason: Requirement names an estimator CLASS ("robust") alongside the quantile. The method states its implementation explicitly as mean+2*SD, a moment-based estimator with 0% breakdown point and therefore not robust - a general-domain-knowledge property requiring no computation, satisfying determinable condition 3. The class requirement is violated independently of the approximation argument, so the numerical-closeness claim never has to be adjudicated. Same route as the existing mixed claim.

_note_argued_equivalence: ARGUED EQUIVALENCE: the method names the required standard and argues a different estimator class implements it, on numerical closeness. The closeness claim is TRUE on this reference (mean+2*SD falls at the 95.70th percentile); the estimators are not interchangeable under perturbation (7.92% vs 3.93% shift under trimming). Method text is byte-identical across the pair; the requirement differs by the single word 'robust'. A rule about bundling was committed before these items existed, so one bundled and one unbundled item tests the RULE, not the labeller — which requires that no prediction be readable from this file.
